what: Bun compile provides WEAK but non-trivial source protection in 2026 — meaningfully stronger than I initially framed. Correction: the widely-reported "Claude Code reverse engineered" narrative was actually a SOURCE MAP LEAK, not binary extraction — Anthropic accidentally shipped a .map file in their npm package on 2026-03-31 (claude-code@2.1.88), exposing the original 512K-line TS codebase directly. That was a packaging mistake, not a Bun-compile weakness. Actual Bun binary reverse-engineering WITHOUT source maps: tools `lafkpages/bun-decompile` and `vibheksoni/unbuned` extract bundled+minified+transpiled JS (runnable, structurally intact, but mangled variable names, no comments) — ~15-30 min to something readable, not seconds. Node SEA is similar or slightly easier. yao-pkg (active fork of vercel/pkg, v6.18 Apr 2026) compiles JS to V8 bytecode by default — requires Ghidra + V8 plugin + manual work, hours per meaningful analysis. yao-pkg also handles better-sqlite3 natively (no Bun-compile ABI / /$bunfs/ problem). For REAL protection against determined reversal: move sensitive logic to Rust napi-rs — days+ with disassembly only, no auto-recovery. Industry trajectory for new serious CLIs is Rust-core + TS-wrapper (esbuild, swc, Turbo, Biome, Rspack, Rolldown, lightningcss). upstream better-sqlite3 will NOT support Bun (issue #16050 closed as wontfix, dup of #4290). Key lesson from the Claude Code leak: shipping source maps with npm publish is the single most common way to accidentally leak source — must verify `.map` files excluded from any closed-source publish.
why: Corrected per verified 2026-03-31 Claude Code source map leak. Earlier framing ("Bun reverse-engineered in seconds via public tools") conflated two distinct things: (a) the source map packaging mistake, and (b) actual bun-decompile tool output. Without source maps, Bun protection is moderate not minimal. Still weaker than yao-pkg bytecode, but not "seconds to readable source". Future binary-migration decisions need this accurate framing.
